title: Accessible inverse images of replete arrow subcategories
statement: Work with small Hom sets in a fixed universe, and colimits as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. A category is locally presentable if it is cocomplete and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa$, generated under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects $P$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves these colimits. Here $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has cardinality less than $\kappa$. Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be locally presentable categories and $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a functor preserving small $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular $\kappa$. Write $\mathcal C^{[1]}$ and $\mathcal D^{[1]}$ for their arrow categories, whose arrows are commuting squares and whose colimits are computed at source and target. A replete full subcategory $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D$ is an accessible subcategory if, for some infinite regular $\lambda$, it is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits computed in $\mathcal D$ and is generated under those colimits by a small set of its objects. Replete means closed under isomorphism in $\mathcal D$. If $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D^{[1]}$ is an accessible subcategory, the replete full subcategory of $\mathcal C^{[1]}$ on arrows $f$ such that $F(f)\in\mathcal V$ is accessible. No assertion is made that the same cardinal works for every $F$ or every $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.7, printed p. 820 (PDF p. 837), applied to the induced functor on arrow categories; the proof of Proposition A.3.7.3 uses exactly this arrow-category instance. No Stacks tag states this accessibility theorem. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\mathcal C^{[1]}$ and $\mathcal B=\mathcal D^{[1]}$. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-monad-presentability] with a singleton set of sorts and the identity monad $T=1$ (unit and multiplication both identities), separately to $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$. Evaluation at the unique sort and formation of one-component families identify the singleton product with the original category, on objects and maps. The identity functor preserves all colimits. Its algebra unit equation $a\circ 1_A=1_A$ forces $a=1_A$, and the morphism equation imposes no condition, so its algebra category identifies with the original category, including every cone and its universal property. The cited completeness conclusion therefore gives pullbacks in $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$. Apply [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability] with the small indexing category $[1]^{\mathrm{op}}$, where $[1]$ has two objects and one nonidentity arrow. Its presheaves are exactly arrows, and its natural transformations are exactly commuting squares: a natural transformation has its two components at the source and target, and its only nonidentity naturality equation is the square equation. Thus $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ are locally presentable in the same smallness universe. The canonical double-opposite identification merely renames objects and arrows, and preserves the colimit and Hom universal properties defining local presentability.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.7 applied on arrow categories, preliminary presentability check; ordinary presheaf theorem in Mathlib Presentable/Presheaf.lean:90-96

proof.text: Let $H=F^{[1]}:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$: on an arrow $f:X\to Y$ it is $F(f):F(X)\to F(Y)$, and on a square $(a,b)$ it is $(F(a),F(b))$. For a small $\kappa$-filtered arrow diagram, compute its colimit at the two endpoints. Preservation by $F$ identifies the two endpoint colimits with the endpoints of the colimit of its $H$-image. Under these two canonical comparisons the arrow maps agree, since their composites with every colimit structure map agree; uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] proves the equality. Hence $H$ preserves these colimits. Let $\mathcal W$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal A$ on $f$ with $H(f)\in\mathcal V$. An isomorphism of arrows is sent to an isomorphism of arrows, so repleteness of $\mathcal V$ implies repleteness of $\mathcal W$.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.7, induced functor on arrow categories: pointwise colimit preservation and repleteness

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-accessible-functor-presentability-ranks] to $H$ to obtain a rank $\rho\geq\kappa$. Let $\lambda$ witness the hypothesis that $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal B$ is accessible. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-subdiagram-criterion] with ambient category $\mathcal B$ and $\sigma=\lambda$: its approximation property holds at all sufficiently large regular $\mu$ with $\lambda\ll\mu$. Choose such a $\mu$ also sharply above $\rho$ and above $\kappa$. This is possible by the arbitrary-large-rank clause of the rank theorem, first using a regular $\sigma\geq\rho,\lambda$. The rank theorem makes $\mathcal B$ locally $\mu$-presentable, so the criterion's moreover clause supplies a small family generating $\mathcal V$ under $\mu$-filtered colimits. Such diagrams are also $\lambda$-filtered, so $\mathcal V$ is closed under them. Likewise a $\mu$-filtered category is $\kappa$-filtered, so $H$ preserves its colimits. For a $\mu$-filtered diagram in $\mathcal W$, its $H$-image lies in $\mathcal V$, and preservation identifies $H$ of its ambient colimit with the colimit of this image. Repleteness and colimit closure of $\mathcal V$ put that colimit back in $\mathcal W$. Thus $\mathcal W$ is closed under small $\mu$-filtered ambient colimits. This proves the needed common-rank assertion; it does not assume arbitrary cardinal enlargement preserves generation.

source.place: Definitions A.2.6.2-3; first paragraph of the proof of Proposition A.2.6.5; Remark 5.4.2.13: choose a common permissible rank

proof.text: We verify the approximation property for $\mathcal W$ at every sufficiently large infinite regular $\tau$ with $\mu\ll\tau$. Since $\rho\leq\mu$, the definition of sharp inequality gives $\rho\ll\tau$. By [lem-coef-accessible-functor-presentability-ranks], $H$ takes $\tau$-presentable objects to $\tau$-presentable objects. Let $I$ be a small $\tau$-filtered poset, $X:I\to\mathcal A$ a diagram of $\tau$-presentable objects with $X_I\in\mathcal W$, and $S\subseteq I$ of size less than $\tau$. Since $I$ is $\kappa$-filtered, preservation gives $\operatorname{colim}_I H(X_i)\cong H(X_I)\in\mathcal V$. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-subdiagram-criterion] to $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal B$, now with $\sigma=\mu$ and the diagram $H X$. Step 3 supplied its small $\mu$-filtered generating family and closure. For all sufficiently large such $\tau$, the criterion supplies a $\tau$-small $\mu$-filtered subset $J\subseteq I$ containing $S$ with $\operatorname{colim}_J H(X_j)\in\mathcal V$. Since $\mu\geq\kappa$, $H$ also preserves this $J$-colimit. Therefore $H(X_J)\cong\operatorname{colim}_J H(X_j)\in\mathcal V$, whence $X_J\in\mathcal W$. The bounds on $\tau$ depend only on the fixed categories, functor and subcategory, not on $I,X,S$.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.5, condition (2 prime)_tau, and the argument underlying Corollary A.2.6.7

proof.text: Step 2 gives repleteness, and step 3 gives closure of $\mathcal W$ under small $\mu$-filtered colimits in the locally presentable ambient category $\mathcal A$. Step 4 establishes condition (ii) of [lem-coef-accessible-subdiagram-criterion] for all sufficiently large regular $\tau$ with $\mu\ll\tau$. Its converse therefore yields a small family generating $\mathcal W$ under small $\mu$-filtered colimits. Together with closure this is exactly accessibility in the statement. The construction selected $\mu$ using $F$ and $\mathcal V$, so it asserts no common cardinal for different inputs.
